title: Cluster-Aware Uncertainty for Polytomous Mokken Scalability
text:
Welcome
This is the replication guide for
It walks through the package that rebuilds every number, figure and table in the paper.
Almost no external data. One thing you need is the mokken package, which carries the application data; everything else ships. Clone, run four commands, and all 15 exhibits rebuild in about five seconds.

title: Cluster-Aware Uncertainty for Polytomous Mokken Scalability
text:
Quick start
Rscript 00_setup.R                          # reports what's missing; installs nothing
Rscript exhibits/00_build_all.R             # 7 figures + 8 floats + the ledger, ~5s
Rscript verification/verify_reproduction.R  # 16 / 16
bash verification/cold_start_rehearsal.sh   # everything, from a bare copy
R ≥ 4.1 and eleven CRAN packages — including mokken, which is required here rather than optional, because the application data SWMDK is distributed inside it and no responses ship with this package.

title: Cluster-Aware Uncertainty for Polytomous Mokken Scalability
text:
What is reproduced

All 15 published exhibits. The eight LaTeX floats are byte-identical to what the paper prints; the seven figures match on page geometry and a fixed-DPI render hash.
The 144-key ledger, byte-identical to the one the manuscript was verified against.
All 69 of the manuscript’s concordance predicates, re-expressed against the rebuilt ledger.

title: Cluster-Aware Uncertainty for Polytomous Mokken Scalability
text:
What is not reproduced
The Phase 16 confirmation and the Phase 17 application. Both ran on AWS; the pipeline ships as annotated reference code and is documented rather than enabled.

title: Cluster-Aware Uncertainty for Polytomous Mokken Scalability
section: One thing to know before reading the code
text:
One thing to know before reading the code
reference-code/R/core/ordinal-h.R ships with a known archival defect and a prominent “do not port” banner. Its transport helper advances on a 1e-12 mass tolerance and can drop a valid tiny positive mass; the corrected kernel is in the bayesmokken package.
No locked result is affected, and this package checks that rather than asserting it: across the 48 locked truth rows, the number with a gap in the open interval (0, 1e-12) — the only condition under which the defect can fire — is zero. See reproducibility.

title: Cluster-Aware Uncertainty for Polytomous Mokken Scalability
text:
Companion package
The binary, independent-respondent case has its own package: bayesmokken-scalability-replication.
Neither depends on the other and they share no data. They do share the verification harness, byte-for-byte, because this package ports it.

title: Cluster-Aware Uncertainty for Polytomous Mokken Scalability
text:
Software and licence
bayesmokken ≥ 0.9.0 implements the method and is pinned, not vendored.
Code is MIT; data, exhibits and this guide are CC BY 4.0. No third-party response data is redistributed.

title: 1  The claim, in one page
text:
1.1 Two population targets, not one estimator
Mokken’s scalability coefficient H is normally computed as if respondents were independent. They often are not: pupils sit in classrooms, patients in clinics, respondents in interviewer caseloads. This paper supplies an interval for polytomous H that accounts for that clustering, and whose coverage has been measured rather than assumed.
The distinction the whole paper turns on, and the first thing the design fixes:
Under informative cluster size — when a cluster’s size is associated with its scalability — these are different population quantities, not two estimators of one thing. Reporting “the” H without saying which is a category error, so the estimand contract requires the target to be declared, never inferred, and every locked summary carries a target column.

title: 1  The claim, in one page
text:
1.2 The method

A two-stage hierarchical Bayesian bootstrap: resample clusters, then respondents within clusters, under a declared weight law.
Compute H exactly under arbitrary weights by finite comonotone transport — not by an approximation that happens to be close.
Tighten the resulting interval by a factor depending on the number of clusters G.

Step 3 runs the opposite way from the companion binary paper, and that is not an accident. The two-stage bootstrap is conservative before calibration — it over-covers — so the correction narrows rather than widens.

title: 1  The claim, in one page
text:
1.5 The boundary
This is a confidence interval, not a posterior credible interval. The hierarchical Bayesian bootstrap is a resampling device; the property claimed is repeated-sampling coverage.
Six phrases the article deliberately never asserts:

“first-ever” · “universally superior” · “new transport theorem” · “credible interval” · “posterior probabilit…” · “analytically derived”

Each occurs in the manuscript only inside a negation or boundary statement, and a frozen claim-eligibility register — 14 claims, written at the source-review gate — governs the article’s wording. It ships as Table H1, and verify_semantics.R asserts all 14 are transcribed.
The comonotone transport result is not claimed as new: CL-03 in that register requires the predecessor credit to Andreadis (2017) to be given.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
2.1 Requirements
The publication-parity build is declared for macOS because the published PDFs were produced with the Quartz device. It requires R ≥ 4.1 and twelve CRAN packages: dplyr, tidyr, readr, ggplot2, scales, patchwork, tibble, ragg, yaml, digest, jsonlite, and mokken.
mokken is required, not optional — unlike in the companion Paper A package. The application data SWMDK is distributed inside it and no responses ship here.
Four command-line tools: pdfinfo, pdftoppm (figure parity), python3 (the disclosure scan), and quarto (the release-gated guide render). bayesmokken is optional.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
2.2 Check the contract first
Rscript 00_setup.R
Reports what is missing and installs nothing. It reads the contract from config.yml, exercises a JSON receipt parse and a one-page Quartz PDF, and checks Quarto, so the declared and executed environment paths cannot drift.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
2.3 Rebuild everything
Rscript exhibits/00_build_all.R
About five seconds: 7 figures (PDF + PNG), 8 LaTeX floats, and the 144-key ledger.






ImportantBuild order matters here for two reasons



01_build_key_numbers.R runs first because it writes the ledger every other generator asserts against — and because it also derives outputs/derived_p16_allcell_summary.csv from the 86,400 raw Phase 16 replication rows, cross-checking it against the locked regular-cell artifact at a 1e-12 tolerance. Both 07_tables.R and 08_osm_figures.R read that file.
The driver enforces the order. Running the generators by hand out of order fails outright rather than silently.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
2.4 Check it reproduced
Rscript verification/verify_reproduction.R
#> 16 / 16 exhibits reproduce
The target is the published manuscript build, not this package’s output.

title: 2  Getting started
section: 2.5 Run everything from a bare copy
text:
2.5 Run everything from a bare copy
bash verification/cold_start_rehearsal.sh
Copies the package to a temporary location, deletes the build outputs, and runs the whole workflow by absolute path from outside the copy, under a directory whose name contains a space. Both details are deliberate: they catch path handling that only works when the working directory happens to be right, and R’s habit of encoding spaces in --file= as ~+~.

text:

Symptom

#> e1257ff16f821ef3cf6c5eed88a91ae2ffa5a067e12603f32c02660d47270797
The digest is of the data frame as loaded; as.matrix(SWMDK) gives a different value, and config.yml records which one the lock means.






Important



If the digest does not match, the mokken you have installed ships different data from the one the application ran on. read_swmdk() stops with both digests and both version numbers. That is a finding about the data source, not something to work around — every application number in the paper is conditional on this object.




3.2.2 Where SWMDK comes from
A documented subset of the Dutch COOL5-18 cohort study, with items from Peetsma and Van der Veen and subset construction following Koopman et al. (2022). None of it is the authors’ to relicense.

title: 3  The frozen data
text:
3.3 The confirmation raw tier
24 per-cell files, 86,400 rows. Load-bearing, not archival: 01_build_key_numbers.R derives the 48-row all-cell summary from it and cross-checks against the locked regular-cell artifact at 1e-12. That summary feeds tabF1_cells.tex and FigF1_cells.pdf.
Selection: candidate == TRUE and gamma_cluster == -1.5 gives 19,200 rows, all with invalid_fraction == 0 and total_draws == 499.
Each cell also ships a truth file, whose minimum_internal_cdf_gap column is what the archival-defect check reads.

title: 3  The frozen data
section: 3.4 A note on paths inside the locked artifacts
text:
3.4 A note on paths inside the locked artifacts
Seventy-five shipped receipts record the project-relative path each file had in the research tree — strings beginning codebase/research/v4/cluster-polytomous/….
Those are provenance, not dependencies. The executable paths registered in provenance/runnable-code.csv do not source, import, execute, or require that tree. Verification is allowed to read copied receipts and archival code as data—for example, to check digests and banners—so a package-wide string search is not the boundary. The paths remain legible because editing locked evidence would break its digests and defeat the point of shipping it.

title: 4  Method notes
text:
4.1 The estimand: declare the target
Under informative cluster size these are different population quantities. v4-estimand-and-sampling-contract-v1.yml requires the target to be declared, and every locked summary carries a target column so a number can never be read without one.
In the SWMDK application the two differ by 0.0024 on the teacher scale (0.6199 respondent-weighted, 0.6223 equal-cluster). Small — and reported separately, because the difference is a property of the population rather than noise to average away.

title: 4  Method notes
section: 4.2 What is conditioned on, and what is resampled
text:
4.2 What is conditioned on, and what is resampled
From the estimand contract:



scale definition
fixed

observed cluster sizes

Cluster sizes are conditioned on, not resampled. That is a modelling choice with consequences for what the interval covers, and it is written down rather than left implicit.

title: 4  Method notes
text:
4.3 Exact H under arbitrary weights
The coefficient is computed by finite comonotone transport — exactly, under whatever weights a bootstrap draw produces, rather than by an approximation that happens to be close for equal weights.






NoteThe transport result is not claimed as new



Claim CL-03 in the frozen register requires the predecessor credit to Andreadis (2017) to be given, and the article never says “new transport theorem”. The contribution is the cluster-aware interval built on it, not the transport identity.


The independent oracle lane checks the implementation against a linear-programming solution of the same problem across an exhaustive grid: 32 configurations, 0 discrepancies.

title: 4  Method notes
section: 4.4 The two-stage bootstrap and why calibration tightens
text:
4.4 The two-stage bootstrap and why calibration tightens
Resample clusters, then respondents within clusters. Before calibration this is conservative — the Phase 16 confirmation measured raw coverage at 99.75 % (respondent) and 99.63 % (equal-cluster) against a nominal 95 %.
So the correction narrows rather than widens: a factor k_G = 1 − 1.5/√G, which for the application’s G = 30 gives 0.7261.






Important



This runs the opposite way from the companion binary paper, whose calibration widens a slightly-short interval. Same idea — a measured correction to a measured miss — in opposite directions, because the two procedures err in opposite directions.
verify_semantics.R asserts the direction (p16_sel_raw_ratio < 1), and one of the negative controls flips it to confirm the check bites.


After calibration: 97.36 % and 97.38 % coverage, at about 75 % of the raw length. Still conservative relative to 95 %, and the paper says so rather than presenting it as exact.

title: 4  Method notes
section: 4.5 Exact knots are disclosures, not errors
text:
4.5 Exact knots are disclosures, not errors
The transport path reports exact-knot counts — configurations where a marginal CDF gap is exactly zero. The article reports these as diagnostic disclosures of the weighted-marginal transport path, not error flags, and the application had 2 on the teacher respondent-weighted lane and 0 on the equal-cluster lane.
They matter for reading the archival defect: the corrected kernel advances on exact zero by design, so an exact knot is a handled case rather than a risk.

title: 4  Method notes
text:
4.6 The claim boundary
Six phrases the article never asserts outside a negation:

“first-ever” · “universally superior” · “new transport theorem” · “credible interval” · “posterior probabilit…” · “analytically derived”

The interval is a confidence interval. The hierarchical Bayesian bootstrap is a resampling device, and the property claimed is repeated-sampling coverage.
A frozen claim-eligibility register of 14 claims, written at the source-review gate, governs the article’s wording. It ships as Table H1; verify_semantics.R asserts all 14 are transcribed into it.

title: 5  The pipeline
text:
5.1 What ran where
Five gates punctuate the evidence chain. reference-code/PIPELINE.md is the full narrative; this is the shape of it.
The order is the argument. The calibration was fitted on training data, tested on held-out data, and only then run on a fresh confirmation — so the confirmation’s coverage numbers are not the numbers the calibration was tuned to.
The Phase 16 confirmation and the Phase 17 application both ran on AWS, with hash-bound protocol locks written before each. Phase 16 wrote 24 per-cell replication files (86,400 rows); Phase 17 wrote 12 draw streams of 99,999 each, 1,199,988 draws in total, with zero invalid draws.

title: 5  The pipeline
text:
5.2 The reference code
reference-code/
  R/core/           ordinal-h.R (SEE BELOW), knot-diagnostics.R
  R/dgp/            the clustered ordinal data-generating processes
  R/evaluation/     intervals, comparators, the Phase 15 calibration
  R/weights/        the two-stage cluster weight law
  phase16/          the confirmation runner, evaluator and finalizer
  phase17/          the application runner, evaluator, finalizer and tests
  tests/            the Phase 14 and 15 test suites, with their receipts
  PIPELINE.md
Nothing in this package sources it. It expects the research tree and an AWS fleet, and keeping it unsourced is what lets it stay faithful to what actually ran — including the defect below.
Every file carries a nine-line archival banner. No code line was changed; ARCHIVAL-DIGESTS.csv records both digests, so tail -n +11 recovers the original — for every file but one, whose authority field was redacted before release and recorded in provenance/redactions.csv.

title: 5  The pipeline
text:
5.3 The archival defect in ordinal-h.R






WarningDo not port this file



reference-code/R/core/ordinal-h.R contains the deterministic per-pair transport helper as it ran. It advances its pointers on a 1e-12 mass tolerance and can drop a valid tiny positive mass. The corrected implementation — exact-zero advancement plus a mass-conservation assertion — is the package kernel: ordinal-transport.R inside the bayesmokken package, which is a separate repository.
The file ships unchanged, with the banner. A replication package that quietly fixes the code it exists to document stops documenting anything.


No locked result is affected, and this package checks it rather than asserting it. See reproducibility for the measurement.

title: 5  The pipeline
section: 5.4 What you can and cannot re-run
text:
5.4 What you can and cannot re-run
Cannot: the confirmation or the application.
Can: everything downstream — exhibits/00_build_all.R in about five seconds.
Can, independently: re-derive the 48-row all-cell summary from the 86,400 raw replication rows, which is exactly what 01_build_key_numbers.R does, with a 1e-12 cross-check against the locked artifact. And recompute the application’s point estimates from data(SWMDK) — the oracle lane does, and reproduces Koopman et al. (2022) while it is there.

Unusual enough to call out. Before integration, the implementation was checked against the published sources it claims to follow — three crosswalks closed across 13 blocking checks, with page- and line-level registers shipping:

title: 8  Governance: what was fixed before what
text:
8.3 The claim-eligibility register
v4-phase18-claim-eligibility-v1.csv, 14 claims, frozen at the source-review gate. It governs the article’s wording: what may be asserted, what must be attributed, and what is out of bounds.
It ships as Table H1, and verify_semantics.R asserts all 14 are transcribed. A results table you can regenerate; a claim register you can only preserve.

title: 8  Governance: what was fixed before what
text:
8.4 The SWMDK lock
The Phase 17 protocol recorded the data object’s digest, version, dimensions and score support before the application ran. Since no responses ship, that lock is what makes the application’s numbers checkable at all — read_swmdk() asserts it on every load.
The digest appears in provenance/excluded-digests.csv with a reason: it is the digest of an R object, not a file, so it resolves to a live check rather than to something on disk.

title: 8  Governance: what was fixed before what
text:
8.5 Two documented departures from byte-identity







What
Register




21 reference-code files bannered
reference-code/ARCHIVAL-DIGESTS.csv


— including ordinal-h.R, with its defect notice
same


10 authority records redacted
provenance/redactions.csv



No code line was changed by the banners. The redactions touched two fields of the authority records: the one naming the command-line harness through which the author’s instruction arrived, and the one that held that instruction verbatim as a short colloquial message. The second is now an English authority token of the same form the companion package uses.
Neither field carried evidence. What each authority actually licensed is in authorized_scope, what it withheld is in explicitly_not_authorized, where it had to stop is in required_stop, and when it was recorded and what it descends from are in recorded_at_utc and parent_governance.sha256. Every one of those is unchanged, and they are what the gate reads.
verify_governance.R accepts the pre-modification digest from either register, which is what lets both departures coexist with a chain that closes.
The rule: a package may modify what it ships only if it records what the file was before.

title: 9  Reproducibility and known limits
text:
9.2 The archival defect
reference-code/R/core/ordinal-h.R ships with a known defect: its transport helper advances on a 1e-12 mass tolerance and can drop a valid tiny positive mass. The corrected kernel lives in the separate bayesmokken package.
The helper compares each current residual atom mass with its tolerance, before and after allocation. Depending on the pointer state, that residual can be an original marginal category mass or a cross-CDF residual. Consequently the exact vulnerable set is inclusive: (0 < ^{-12}).
The claim is that no locked result is affected. This package checks it by direct execution. verification/archival/verify_archival_safety.R rebuilds all 168 population-truth configurations that called this helper: 36 Phase 14, 48 Phase 15 training, 36 Phase 15 validation, and 48 Phase 16.
Across those 168 configurations:



residuals in (0, 1e-12]
0


smallest positive marginal category mass
0.0155404871882598


smallest positive cross-CDF gap
1.93915947650503e-05


maximum abs(old H - corrected H)
0


corrected-kernel mass-conservation failures
0



Literal zero is safe: the old <= check advances it, and simultaneous exact exhaustion advances both pointers. The Phase 16 table has eight rows whose scalar minimum is zero; that is not a count of literal zero gaps. The full certificate records all positive marginal masses, all positive cross-CDF gaps, and direct old/corrected results instead of treating one scalar minimum as a complete risk certificate.
The verifier also runs synthetic fixtures at 0.5e-12, exactly 1e-12, and just above 1e-12, plus an edge-mass case and literal-zero case. The first two inclusive risk cases make old and corrected results diverge; the above-boundary and literal-zero cases agree.
Per-replication point and bootstrap-draw calculations use the survival/pmin kernel and bypass the defective helper. The helper was used for deterministic population truths; the 168-row certificate therefore covers every locked execution path to which this particular defect applies.

The direction control matters here because this calibration tightens while the companion paper’s widens. A check that merely asserted “the calibration changes the length” would pass on either, and would be worthless.

title: 9  Reproducibility and known limits
text:
9.5 Known limits
Cross-platform raster identity. Figure parity hashes a pdftoppm render at 150 dpi, so the hash depends on the Poppler build. Matching geometry with differing pixels is more likely a renderer difference than a scientific one.
This reproduces the analysis snapshot, not the production runs. The Phase 16 confirmation and Phase 17 application ran on AWS and are documented, not enabled.
The application data is not ours to ship. Every application number is conditional on the SWMDK object in your mokken install. The lock makes a mismatch loud rather than silent, but it cannot prevent one.
The receipt chain is scoped to the v4 receipts; see governance.
The manuscript-text checks live with the manuscript — the needle half of each concordance check, and the six-phrase claim-boundary audit, run where the .tex is.

title: 9  Reproducibility and known limits
text:
9.6 Two traps worth knowing
grep silently skips Latin-1 TeX logs as binary — zero hits can mean “did not read”. Use grep -a.
data.table::fread() given a .gz path decompresses it in place, mutating the frozen snapshot. The readers here open gzfile() connections.

title: 10  Artifact index
text:
10.3 Three conventions
Absolute paths live in one file — common/R/paths.R, which contains none itself.
reference-code/ is never sourced or executed by the registered runnable layer. Verification may read it as text/data to check digests, banners, and the archival-safety certificate. verification/verify_quarantine.py audits the source/import/subprocess boundary, and a cold build is rehearsed with the whole directory unavailable.
The runnable build does not depend on the companion paper’s research tree. The copied receipts and archival evidence legitimately retain those provenance strings; they are outside this narrower execution claim. The exact public file set is checked against provenance/release-files.csv.
